solutions.title: Fill from the back
solutions.notes: Three pointers from the back — O(1) extra
solutions.description:
**Approach:** Fill `nums1` from index `m+n-1` downward, always taking the larger of `nums1[i]` / `nums2[j]`.

**Complexity:** Time **O(m+n)**, space **O(1)**.

**Why preferred:** Uses the spare tail of `nums1` so you never shift elements.

solutions.title: Forward splice from nums2
solutions.description:
**Approach:** Walk `nums1`; when `nums2` value should go first, `splice` it in and `pop` a trailing zero slot.

**Complexity:** Each `splice` is **O(m+n)** → overall roughly **O((m+n)·n)` worst case.

**vs recommended:** Harder to reason about indices and slower. Filling from the back is the intended in-place merge.
